title: Continuity tokens and partial-snapshot chunking for safe SSE reconnects
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Users/clients commonly experience mid-stream disconnects (network flaps, mobile sleep, proxy timeouts). Current resume approaches either require clients to re-request from the start or depend on conservative server-side checkpoints that increase latency. This ticket proposes a lightweight continuity metadata layer + partial-snapshot envelopes that allow safe, idempotent reconnect and limited replay without changing customer-visible message semantics or instrumenting every model.

Goals:
- Add a compact continuity token and offset hints embedded in SSE event envelopes so clients can request a minimal delta on reconnect.
- Define a partial-snapshot chunk envelope that preserves function-call boundaries and structured output atomicity (no split JSON objects across reconnects).
- Provide a backward-compatible server-side shim so legacy SSE clients ignore extra fields and newer SDKs auto-resume with minimal rehydration.
- Keep run-time overhead < 3% p99 latency and avoid additional round-trips for the common fast-path.

Out of scope:
- Full persistent transcript store (separate infra ticket).
- Complex multi-tenant cross-region state replication (tacked under Dedicated routing).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits continuity_token and chunk_offset metadata in SSE event envelopes when enabled
Client SDK can reconnect and request delta since last-seen continuity_token, receiving only missing chunks
Function call frames remain atomic after reconnect and never duplicate side-effectful function-call execution
Legacy SSE clients (no continuity_token handling) continue to receive a valid stream without protocol errors
End-to-end performance benchmarks show <3% p99 latency regression with continuity metadata enabled
tasks: Design wire format for continuity metadata and partial-snapshot chunk envelopes
Implement server-side encoder that emits chunk envelopes and continuity_token per stream window
Extend SDK (node/python) to support auto-reconnect using continuity_token and fetch-delta endpoint
Add compatibility shim: server accepts legacy reconnect requests and can return full fallback payloads
Create integration tests that simulate mid-stream disconnect and validate no double-function-call triggers
Benchmark latency and memory impact with 1000 concurrent streams and report results
design_notes:
Wire-format proposal (compact SSE envelope):
- event: 'chunk'
- data: JSONL line containing { 'id': '<chunk-id>', 'offset': 12345, 'continuity_token': 'ct_v1:abc...', 'boundary_hint': 'atomic' , 'payload': '<base64-or-raw>' }
Rationale: single-line JSON avoids multi-line SSE framing pitfalls for many clients.

Partial-snapshot rules:
- When payload contains structured JSON, server must never split inside a top-level value. If a chunk would split an object/array, we instead emit a small snapshot header with 'boundary_hint':'atomic' and buffer until the boundary is reached.

Reconnect flow (high-level):
1) Client sees disconnect after last chunk id X and stores continuity_token T.
2) Client calls /v1/streams/{stream_id}/resume?token=T&after=X (SDK helper).
3) Server verifies token validity window (configurable TTL) and streams only missing chunks, or if token expired returns full catch-up snapshot labeled 'fallback_full_transcript'.
Compatibility shim: servers must include HTTP header 'X-Continuity-Support: v1' when the feature is active. Legacy clients ignore unknown headers and continue consuming SSE normally.

Security considerations: continuity_token encodes stream version and a short HMAC. Token TTL defaults to 2 minutes; configurable per-customer. Longer retention requires enterprise opt-in and audit logging.
